subproblem.title: Graph coordinates: continuity, the first-block map a, and the rotated graph images over closed and open balls
subproblem.statement: For all natural numbers n, l and every linear isometry q of R^{n+l}, let a(z) := (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q^{-1} z)).1 in R^n (the first n coordinates of q^{-1} z). Then: (i) (x, y) |-> graphPoint x y is continuous from R^n x R^l (product topology) to R^{n+l}; (ii) a is continuous; (iii) a(q(graphPoint x y)) = x for all x in R^n and y in R^l; (iv) for every f : R^n -> R^l continuous on the closed ball B^n_R(0) (nothing is assumed off the ball) and all reals r <= R, the set q(graph f over B^n_R(0)) = q '' graphOver f (closedBall 0 R) is compact, and the set q(graph f over the open ball B°^n_r(0)) = q '' graphOver f (ball 0 r) is a Borel subset of R^{n+l} (MeasurableSet for Mathlib's Borel measurable structure on EuclideanSpace).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ), Continuous (fun p : Rn n × Rn ℓ => graphPoint p.1 p.2) ∧ Continuous (fun z : Amb n ℓ => (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q.symm z)).1) ∧ (∀ (x : Rn n) (y : Rn ℓ), (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q.symm (q (graphPoint x y)))).1 = x) ∧ ∀ (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (R r : ℝ), ContinuousOn f (closedBall 0 R) → r ≤ R → IsCompact (q '' graphOver f (closedBall 0 R)) ∧ MeasurableSet (q '' graphOver f (ball 0 r))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This child is steps 1(i), 1(ii) and 2(iii) of the proof of gwe_graph_tangential_estimate.
- The parent applies (iv) with R = sigma/2, r = sigma/4 and f 1-Lipschitz, hence continuous, on B^n_{sigma/2}(0). This gives Gamma compact (so Borel) and Gamma' Borel.
- (i) and (ii) give the continuity of x |-> q(graphPoint (grad zeta(a(x))) 0).
- (iii) is a(F(x')) = x'.
No extra import is needed.

Notation. By definition graphPoint x y = toLp 2 (Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y)). EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd is a continuous linear equivalence R^{n+l} -> R^n x R^l. It reindexes along finSumFinEquiv.symm and then splits R^{Fin n + Fin l} into R^n x R^l. For f and a set D, write F(x) := q(graphPoint x (f x)).

1. Coordinates of a graph point: finAddEquivProd(graphPoint x y) = (x, y). Compare coordinates (ext), for each component of the pair.
 - For i in Fin n, the i-th coordinate of the first component is Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y) (Fin.castAdd l i) = x_i (Fin.append_left).
 - For k in Fin l, the k-th coordinate of the second component is Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y) (Fin.natAdd n k) = y_k (Fin.append_right).
 Both are direct simp computations after unfolding graphPoint and finAddEquivProd.
2. Proof of (i). Apply the inverse equivalence to step 1 (ContinuousLinearEquiv.eq_symm_apply): graphPoint x y = finAddEquivProd.symm (x, y) for every pair (x, y). The inverse of a continuous linear equivalence is continuous. Hence (x, y) |-> graphPoint x y = finAddEquivProd.symm (x, y) is continuous.
3. Proof of (ii). a = Prod.fst o finAddEquivProd o q^{-1}. This is a composition of continuous maps: q^{-1} is a linear isometry, finAddEquivProd is a continuous linear equivalence, and fst is continuous.
4. Proof of (iii). Since q^{-1}(q(w)) = w (LinearIsometryEquiv.symm_apply_apply), step 1 gives a(q(graphPoint x y)) = (finAddEquivProd(graphPoint x y)).1 = (x, y).1 = x.
5. Proof of (iv), compactness. Let f be continuous on B^n_R(0) and r <= R.
 - For every set D, q '' graphOver f D = F '' D, since graphOver f D is the image of D under x |-> graphPoint x (f x) (Set.image_image).
 - F is continuous on B^n_R(0): x |-> (x, f(x)) is continuous on the ball because f is (ContinuousOn.prodMk with continuousOn_id); then compose with the continuous map of (i) and with the continuous q.
 - The closed ball B^n_R(0) is compact, since R^n is proper (isCompact_closedBall). The image of a compact set under a map continuous on it is compact (IsCompact.image_of_continuousOn). So F(B^n_R(0)) is compact.
6. Proof of (iv), Borel set. Claim: F(B°^n_r(0)) = F(B^n_R(0)) cap a^{-1}(B°^n_r(0)).
 - Inclusion from left to right. Let x be in B°_r(0). Then |x| < r <= R, so x is in B_R(0). By (iii), a(F(x)) = x lies in B°_r(0).
 - Inclusion from right to left. Let z = F(x) with x in B_R(0) and a(z) in B°_r(0). By (iii), x = a(F(x)) = a(z) lies in B°_r(0). So z is in F(B°_r(0)).
 F(B_R(0)) is compact by step 5, hence closed in the Hausdorff space R^{n+l}, hence Borel. a^{-1}(B°_r(0)) is open by (ii), hence Borel. Their intersection is Borel. QED
proof_key_steps: finAddEquivProd(graphPoint x y) = (x, y) by coordinates (Fin.append_left/right); hence graphPoint x y = finAddEquivProd.symm (x, y), which gives (i).
(ii): a = fst o finAddEquivProd o q^{-1} is continuous; (iii): a(q(graphPoint x y)) = (finAddEquivProd(graphPoint x y)).1 = x.
(iv): F(x) = q(graphPoint x (f x)) is continuous on the compact ball B_R(0), so F(B_R(0)) = q '' graphOver f (closedBall 0 R) is compact.
(iv): by (iii) and r <= R, F(B°_r(0)) = F(B_R(0)) cap a^{-1}(B°_r(0)) = closed cap open, hence Borel.

The open-ball graph equals the compact graph intersected with the inverse image of the open ball, proving Borel measurability. No unstated global continuity or radius positivity is needed.

subproblem.title: Lipschitz maps on a closed ball: Rademacher null set, derivative bound and gradient rows
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, K >= 0 (K in R_{>=0}), R real, and f : R^n -> R^l K-Lipschitz on the closed ball B^n_R(0) (nothing is assumed off the ball). Let Z := {x in B°^n_R(0) : f is not (Frechet) differentiable at x}, where B°^n_R(0) is the open ball. Then: (i) Z is a Borel set (MeasurableSet); (ii) L^n(Z) = 0, where L^n is Lebesgue measure (volume) on R^n; (iii) for every x in B°^n_R(0): ||Df(x)|| <= K (operator norm, Df(x) = fderiv R f x, which is 0 where f is not differentiable), and if f is differentiable at x then, for every j in Fin l and every v in R^n, <grad f^j(x), v> = (Df(x) v)_j, where f^j = (y |-> (f y)_j) is the j-th coordinate function of f and grad = gradient (the Riesz representative of the derivative).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (K : ℝ≥0) (R : ℝ), LipschitzOnWith K f (closedBall 0 R) → MeasurableSet (ball (0 : Rn n) R ∩ {x | ¬DifferentiableAt ℝ f x}) ∧ volume (ball (0 : Rn n) R ∩ {x | ¬DifferentiableAt ℝ f x}) = 0 ∧ ∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) R, ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤ K ∧ (DifferentiableAt ℝ f x → ∀ (j : Fin ℓ) (v : Rn n), inner ℝ (gradient (fun y => f y j) x) v = fderiv ℝ f x v j)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This child is the first bullet of step 8 and the second and third bullets of step 9 of the proof of gwe_graph_tangential_estimate. The parent applies it with K = 1 and R = sigma/2. No extra import is needed.

Notation. B := B^n_R(0) is the closed ball and B° := B°^n_R(0) the open ball. D := {x in R^n : f is differentiable at x}, so Z = B° cap D^c. For j in Fin l, pi_j := EuclideanSpace.proj j : R^l -> R is the j-th coordinate map. It is continuous and linear, and f^j = pi_j o f.

1. Proof of (i). For an arbitrary map f from a normed space with its Borel structure into a complete normed space, the set of differentiability points is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt). No continuity of f and no finite dimension are needed; R^l is complete. So D is Borel, and so is D^c. The open ball B° is Borel. Hence Z = B° cap D^c is Borel.
2. Proof of (ii).
 - B° is contained in B, so f is K-Lipschitz on B° (LipschitzOnWith.mono).
 - By Rademacher's theorem (LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem, for Lebesgue measure on R^n, an additive Haar measure): for L^n-a.e. x, if x is in B° then f is differentiable within B° at x.
 - B° is open, so it is a neighbourhood of each of its points. So differentiability within B° at x is differentiability at x (DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt).
 - Hence for L^n-a.e. x we have x not in Z: if x were in Z, then x would be in B°, f would be differentiable at x, and x would be in D. By measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem, L^n(Z) = 0.
3. Proof of (iii), derivative bound. Let x be in B°. The open ball B° is a neighbourhood of x and lies in B, so B is a neighbourhood of x (mem_of_superset). A map that is K-Lipschitz on a neighbourhood of x satisfies ||fderiv R f x|| <= K (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn). This needs no differentiability: if f is not differentiable at x, then fderiv R f x = 0.
4. Proof of (iii), gradient rows. Assume f is differentiable at x, and fix j and v.
 - pi_j is continuous linear, so it is its own derivative everywhere. By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp), f^j = pi_j o f has derivative pi_j o Df(x) at x. Hence fderiv R f^j x = pi_j composed with Df(x).
 - By definition gradient f^j x = (toDual R R^n)^{-1}(fderiv R f^j x).
 - For every continuous linear functional L, <(toDual)^{-1} L, v> = L v (InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply).
 Hence <grad f^j(x), v> = pi_j(Df(x) v) = (Df(x) v)_j. QED
proof_key_steps: (i): {x | DifferentiableAt R f x} is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt), so Z = ball cap its complement is Borel.
(ii): Rademacher (LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem) on the open ball, where differentiability within the ball equals differentiability; so a.e. x is not in Z and L^n(Z) = 0.
(iii): B_R(0) is a neighbourhood of every point of the open ball, so ||fderiv R f x|| <= K (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn).
(iii): f^j = proj_j o f, so by the chain rule fderiv f^j x = proj_j o Df(x); <(toDual)^{-1} L, v> = L v gives <grad f^j(x), v> = (Df(x) v)_j.

The neighborhood Lipschitz bound also covers the total fderiv convention at nondifferentiability points. The coordinate chain rule and Riesz identity prove the gradient-row formula. subproblem.title: Localization of a set integral to a good set with a pointwise comparison (abstract measure theory)
subproblem.statement: Let X be a type (in Lean's lowest universe, Type) with a measurable structure and a measure mu. Let B, B', G, G' be subsets of X, Phi, phi, psi : X -> R, M >= 0 real and m in [0, infinity]. Assume: (1) G and G' are measurable; (2) G' is contained in B and in B'; (3) Phi is mu-integrable on B; (4) |Phi(x)| <= M for every x in X; (5) Phi(x) = 0 for every x in (B \ G') cap G; (6) mu((B \ G') \ G) <= m and m < infinity; (7) phi is a.e. strongly measurable for mu restricted to G'; (8) psi is mu-integrable on B' and psi(x) >= 0 for every x; (9) for mu-a.e. x, x in G' implies |Phi(x) - phi(x)| <= M psi(x). Then |int_{G'} phi dmu| <= |int_B Phi dmu| + M m.toReal + M int_{B'} psi dmu (Bochner set integrals; the proof also shows that phi is mu-integrable on G').
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {X : Type} [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (B B' G G' : Set X) (Φ φ ψ : X → ℝ) (M : ℝ) (m : ℝ≥0∞), 0 ≤ M → MeasurableSet G → MeasurableSet G' → G' ⊆ B → G' ⊆ B' → IntegrableOn Φ B μ → (∀ x, |Φ x| ≤ M) → (∀ x ∈ (B \ G') ∩ G, Φ x = 0) → μ ((B \ G') \ G) ≤ m → m < ⊤ → AEStronglyMeasurable φ (μ.restrict G') → IntegrableOn ψ B' μ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ ψ x) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ G' → |Φ x - φ x| ≤ M * ψ x) → |∫ x in G', φ x ∂μ| ≤ |∫ x in B, Φ x ∂μ| + M * m.toReal + M * ∫ x in B', ψ x ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This child is steps 5, 6, 7 (first half), 10 and 11 of the proof of gwe_graph_tangential_estimate, stated for an abstract measure space. In step 6 the vanishing of Phi on (B \ Gamma') cap Gamma is now hypothesis (5). The parent applies it with:
- X = R^{n+l}, mu = V.weight;
- B = B_{sigma/2}(0), B' = B_sigma(0), G = Gamma, G' = Gamma';
- Phi = the integrand of gwe_vertical_first_variation, phi = <grad f^j(a), grad zeta(a)>, psi = |p - P|^2;
- m = mu(B_{sigma/2}(0) cap (spt V \ Gamma)).
The hypothesis M >= 0 cannot be dropped: if X is empty, (4) holds for a negative M, and the claim fails when m > 0. No extra import is needed. All integrals are Bochner set integrals against mu.

1. First split. G' is measurable and Phi is integrable on B. By integral_inter_add_sdiff,
 int_{B cap G'} Phi + int_{B \ G'} Phi = int_B Phi,
 and B cap G' = G' by (2).
2. Second split. Phi is integrable on B \ G', a subset of B (IntegrableOn.mono_set). G is measurable, so integral_inter_add_sdiff gives
 int_{(B \ G') cap G} Phi + int_{(B \ G') \ G} Phi = int_{B \ G'} Phi.
3. Vanishing part. By (5), int_{(B \ G') cap G} Phi = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero). With steps 1 and 2,
 int_{G'} Phi = int_B Phi - int_{(B \ G') \ G} Phi.
4. Off part.
 - mu((B \ G') \ G) <= m < infinity by (6), so this set has finite measure.
 - By (4), ||Phi(x)|| <= M on it. So norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const gives |int_{(B \ G') \ G} Phi| <= M mu.real((B \ G') \ G). Here mu.real s = (mu s).toReal by definition (Measure.real), so the bound is M mu((B \ G') \ G).toReal.
 - Since m != infinity, ENNReal.toReal_mono gives mu((B \ G') \ G).toReal <= m.toReal. With M >= 0, |int_{(B \ G') \ G} Phi| <= M m.toReal.
5. Integrability on G'.
 - Phi is integrable on G' (a subset of B), and psi is integrable on G' (a subset of B').
 - Phi - phi is a.e. strongly measurable for mu restricted to G'. Phi's integrability gives this for Phi, and (7) gives it for phi.
 - G' is measurable, so (9) yields ||Phi(x) - phi(x)|| <= M psi(x) for a.e. x with respect to mu restricted to G' (ae_restrict_iff').
 - M psi is integrable on G'. By domination (Integrable.mono'), Phi - phi is integrable on G'. Hence phi = Phi - (Phi - phi) is integrable on G'.
6. Comparison.
 - Both are integrable, so int_{G'} Phi - int_{G'} phi = int_{G'} (Phi - phi) (integral_sub).
 - By the a.e. bound of step 5, norm_integral_le_of_norm_le and integral_const_mul give |int_{G'} (Phi - phi)| <= int_{G'} M psi = M int_{G'} psi.
 - psi >= 0 is integrable on B' and G' is contained in B'. So int_{G'} psi <= int_{B'} psi (setIntegral_mono_set). As M >= 0, |int_{G'} Phi - int_{G'} phi| <= M int_{B'} psi.
7. Conclusion.
 |int_{G'} phi| <= |int_{G'} Phi| + |int_{G'} Phi - int_{G'} phi|, by the triangle inequality;
 <= |int_B Phi| + |int_{(B \ G') \ G} Phi| + M int_{B'} psi, by step 3, the triangle inequality and step 6;
 <= |int_B Phi| + M m.toReal + M int_{B'} psi, by step 4. QED
proof_key_steps: Split int_B Phi along G' and then along G (integral_inter_add_sdiff, using G, G' measurable and Phi integrable on B); the (B \ G') cap G part vanishes by (5), so int_{G'} Phi = int_B Phi - int_{(B \ G') \ G} Phi.
Off part: |int_{(B \ G') \ G} Phi| <= M mu((B \ G') \ G).toReal <= M m.toReal (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const, toReal_mono, M >= 0).
Phi - phi is a.e. strongly measurable on G' and dominated by M psi there, so it is integrable on G' (Integrable.mono'); hence phi is integrable on G'.
|int_{G'} Phi - int_{G'} phi| = |int_{G'} (Phi - phi)| <= M int_{G'} psi <= M int_{B'} psi (setIntegral_mono_set, psi >= 0).

subproblem.title: Tangent projections are contractions; tangent-projection integrands are integrable on sets of finite weight
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U an arbitrary subset of R^{n+l}, V a rectifiable n-varifold in U, mu := V.weight and p_x := V.tangentProj x (a continuous linear map of R^{n+l}). Then: (a) ||p_x v|| <= ||v|| for all x, v in R^{n+l}; (b) if x |-> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable (as a map into the space of continuous linear maps R^{n+l} -> R^{n+l} with the operator norm), then for every set S of R^{n+l} with mu(S) < infinity: (b1) for every e in R^{n+l}, every mu-a.e. strongly measurable g : R^{n+l} -> R^{n+l} and every real C with ||g(x)|| <= C for all x, the function x |-> <p_x e, p_x g(x)> is mu-integrable on S; (b2) for every linear subspace T of R^{n+l}, the function x |-> |p_x - p_T|^2 := hsNormSq(p_x - T.starProjection) is mu-integrable on S.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), (∀ x v : Amb n ℓ, ‖V.tangentProj x v‖ ≤ ‖v‖) ∧ (AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight → ∀ S : Set (Amb n ℓ), V.weight S < ⊤ → (∀ (e : Amb n ℓ) (g : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (C : ℝ), AEStronglyMeasurable g V.weight → (∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ C) → IntegrableOn (fun x => inner ℝ (V.tangentProj x e) (V.tangentProj x (g x))) S V.weight) ∧ ∀ T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), IntegrableOn (fun x => hsNormSq (V.tangentProj x - T.starProjection)) S V.weight)

Context. This child is step 1(iii) and step 3 of the proof of gwe_graph_tangential_estimate. The parent applies (b1) with S = B_{sigma/2}(0), e = e'_j, g(x) = q(graphPoint (grad zeta(a(x))) 0) and C = M. It applies (b2) with S = B_sigma(0) and T = rotatedPlane q. No extra import is needed.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i in Fin(n + l); these vectors have norm 1. For a linear subspace T, P_T := T.starProjection. hsNormSq A = sum_i ||A e_i||^2.

1. Proof of (a). By the definition of V.tangentProj, p_x is either K.starProjection for some linear subspace K (the subspace chosen by Classical.choose when an approximate tangent space exists) or the zero map.
 - In the first case ||K.starProjection|| <= 1 (Submodule.starProjection_norm_le). Hence ||p_x v|| <= ||p_x|| ||v|| <= ||v|| (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm).
 - In the second case p_x v = 0, and ||0|| = 0 <= ||v||.
2. For (b), assume that x |-> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, and let mu(S) < infinity.
3. (b1), measurability. Consider Psi(L, w) := <L e, L w> on (R^{n+l} ->L R^{n+l}) x R^{n+l}.
 - (L, w) |-> L e and (L, w) |-> L w are continuous, since evaluation of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous (Continuous.clm_apply).
 - The inner product is continuous, so Psi is continuous.
 - Both x |-> p_x and g are mu-a.e. strongly measurable. Hence x |-> Psi(p_x, g(x)) = <p_x e, p_x g(x)> is mu-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
4. (b1), bound. For every x, |<p_x e, p_x g(x)>| <= ||p_x e|| ||p_x g(x)|| <= ||e|| ||g(x)|| <= ||e|| C. This uses Cauchy-Schwarz (abs_real_inner_le_norm), then (a) twice, then the hypothesis on g.
5. (b1), integrability. A mu-a.e. strongly measurable function that is bounded by a constant on a set of finite mu-measure is integrable on that set (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded with mu(S) != infinity and the constant ||e|| C).
6. (b2), measurability.
 - A |-> hsNormSq(A) = sum_i ||A e_i||^2 is continuous on R^{n+l} ->L R^{n+l}: it is a finite sum of squares of norms of the continuous evaluations A |-> A e_i.
 - x |-> p_x - P_T is mu-a.e. strongly measurable (a measurable map minus a constant).
 - Hence x |-> hsNormSq(p_x - P_T) is mu-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable).
7. (b2), bound. hsNormSq(p_x - P_T) >= 0, as a sum of squares. Fix i.
 - ||p_x e_i|| <= ||e_i|| = 1 by (a).

subproblem.title: Varifold weight: finite on compact subsets of U, null off spt V, absolutely continuous with respect to H^n
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U an arbitrary subset of R^{n+l} (no openness is assumed), and V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (the contract structure RectifiableVarifold), with M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, H^n := muHE[n] on R^{n+l} and weight mu := V.weight = (H^n restricted to M).withDensity (ofReal o theta). Then: (i) mu(K) < infinity for every compact set K contained in U; (ii) mu(R^{n+l} \ spt V) = 0, where spt V = V.support = U cap supp(mu); (iii) every set Z of R^{n+l} with H^n(Z) = 0 (Z arbitrary, not necessarily measurable) satisfies mu(Z) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), (∀ K : Set (Amb n ℓ), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → V.weight K < ⊤) ∧ V.weight (V.support)ᶜ = 0 ∧ ∀ Z : Set (Amb n ℓ), (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) Z = 0 → V.weight Z = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This child is step 2(i), step 2(ii) and the absolute continuity mu << H^n used in step 8 of the proof of gwe_graph_tangential_estimate. It uses only the definitions RectifiableVarifold.weight and RectifiableVarifold.support and the structure fields carrier_subset, nullMeasurableSet_carrier and integrableOn_mult. No extra import is needed.

Notation. H := muHE[n] on R^{n+l}, M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, rho(x) := ofReal(theta(x)), H|M := H.restrict M. By definition mu = V.weight = (H|M).withDensity rho, and spt V = V.support = U cap mu.support.

1. Absolute continuity. A measure with density is absolutely continuous with respect to its base measure, so mu << H|M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous). A restriction is below the measure, H|M <= H (Measure.restrict_le_self), hence H|M << H (Measure.absolutelyContinuous_of_le). By transitivity, mu << H.
2. Proof of (iii). Let H(Z) = 0. By step 1, mu(Z) = 0. Absolute continuity of measures is a statement about all sets, so no measurability of Z is needed.
3. Proof of (i). Let K be compact with K contained in U.
 a. K is closed, since R^{n+l} is Hausdorff (IsCompact.isClosed). Hence K is Borel.
 b. Since K is measurable, withDensity_apply gives mu(K) = int^-_K rho d(H|M), the lower integral of rho against (H|M) restricted to K.
 c. Since K is measurable, Measure.restrict_restrict gives (H|M) restricted to K = H restricted to K cap M. So mu(K) = int^-_{K cap M} rho dH, and K cap M = M cap K.
 d. The field V.integrableOn_mult applied to K (compact, K contained in U) says theta is H-integrable on M cap K. In particular its finite-integral part gives int^-_{M cap K} ||theta||_e dH < infinity.
 e. For every x, rho(x) = ofReal(theta(x)) <= ofReal(|theta(x)|) = ||theta(x)||_e, because theta(x) <= |theta(x)|.
 f. By monotonicity of the lower integral, mu(K) <= int^-_{M cap K} ||theta||_e dH < infinity.
4. Proof of (ii). The complement of spt V = U cap mu.support is U^c cup (mu.support)^c (compl_inter). So it suffices to show that both pieces are mu-null (measure_union_null).
 a. mu((mu.support)^c) = 0 by Measure.measure_compl_support. Its hypothesis HereditarilyLindelofSpace holds because R^{n+l} is second countable.
 b. mu(U^c) = 0. By step 1 it suffices that (H|M)(U^c) = 0. M is H-null-measurable (V.nullMeasurableSet_carrier), so Measure.restrict_apply₀' gives (H|M)(U^c) = H(U^c cap M). Since M is contained in U (V.carrier_subset), U^c cap M is empty, and H of the empty set is 0.
 c. Hence mu((spt V)^c) = 0. QED
proof_key_steps: mu = (H^n|M).withDensity(ofReal theta) << H^n|M << H^n (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous, absolutelyContinuous_of_le restrict_le_self); this is (iii).
(i): K compact => closed => Borel; mu(K) = int^-_{M cap K} ofReal(theta) dH^n (withDensity_apply, restrict_restrict) <= int^-_{M cap K} ||theta||_e dH^n < infinity by V.integrableOn_mult.
(ii): (spt V)^c = U^c cup (supp mu)^c; mu((supp mu)^c) = 0 (measure_compl_support); mu(U^c) = 0 since (H^n|M)(U^c) = H^n(U^c cap M) = H^n(empty) by restrict_apply₀' and M subset U.
